findings.humor_and_voices: Neet converts cleaning into a military emergency and treats yesterday’s Cheerio as property; Buddy has his own sock-protection objective, resents orders that duplicate his own decision, carefully hides his bark and then performs a useless full encirclement. The comic distinction survives the full reading. Sagar’s practical Cheerio answer and threatened repeat vacuum contrast with Heather’s firm breakfast priority.
findings.timing_and_cause_effect: The pre-plug-in retreat precedes the roar, kitchen movement grows from crumb defense, and ordinary completion becomes the dogs’ victory. Neet immediately soils the clean rug, paying off the humans’ actual goal. The separate lines for both dogs turning and Heather refusing give the reversal room.
findings.ending_and_affection: Breakfast naturally follows Heather’s decision. Buddy’s eyewitness correction punctures the boast and Neet’s cord accusation restores his theatrical self-image. The evening ottoman return closes the opening domestic frame and the closet menace supplies a light final callback without undermining household warmth.
image_placement: Sock remains in Buddy’s mouth before it is deposited on the couch; the vacuum cord is stored and Neet barks before Act III activation.
Kitchen panel follows Buddy joining the action after securing his sock; bowl, loose crumb and slack cord support the confrontation. Neither sock nor mud is prematurely present.
Muddy panel comes immediately after Buddy stops and looks down, before his sidestep and Heather lifting the rug. Neet’s proud stance contrasts with the obvious tracks, and Buddy stays on clean floor.
